subject: candle flame
title: A Candle Flame Makes 1.5 Million Diamonds a Second, Then Burns Them

scenes.text: Every candle you've ever lit was making diamonds.
Not one or two. About one and a half million diamond particles every second, inside an ordinary flame.
It started as a dare. A colleague told chemist Wuzong Zhou at St Andrews that nobody really knew what was inside a flame.
So in 2011 he pulled particles from the flame's centre with a special filter and put them under an electron microscope.
All four forms of carbon were there, including diamond crystals a few nanometres across. The flame builds them, then its tip burns them into carbon dioxide.
Made and destroyed in a fraction of a second, millions at a time. Every candle, a diamond factory you can blow out.

description:
A candle flame creates about 1.5 million diamond nanoparticles every second.
In 2011, Professor Wuzong Zhou of the University of St Andrews sampled the centre of a burning candle flame and found all four known forms of carbon, including diamond nanoparticles. They form in the flame and are burned away into carbon dioxide at the top, so none survive. The work was published in Chemical Communications.
What everyday thing do you think is hiding a surprise like this?
first_comment: Michael Faraday lectured on the chemistry of a candle in 1860, and it still took until 2011 to find the diamonds in it. What other everyday object do you think science has not fully explained yet?
